item.title: Hundreds attend Roscommon concert
item.description: Hundreds of people attended a free Christmas concert in Roscommon on Friday night - as a school said 'thank you' to the local community. The Roscommon Solstice Choir performed in Whitehall Church in Tarmonbarry. It was for Cloonfour National School nearby. item.title: Calls for back-up to emergency communication supply
item.description: A Roscommon councillor has called for a back up power supply to be provided for Fire Services Emergency Communications in the event of future storms. Independent Cllr Micheal Frain raised the issue at today’s Roscommon County Council meeting. He says during Storm Éowyn, the TETRA communication system went down due to power outages across the region. item.title: Urgent call for respite beds at Ballinamore Community Hospital
item.description: The HSE is facing calls to provide additional respite capicity at Ballinamore Community Hospital. With ongoing concerns over overcrowding at larger facilities, it's felt supports closer to home may offer vital short-term relief to families. Councillor Ita Reynolds Flynn tabled the motion at this month's meeting of the local municipal district. item.title: Hot Air Ballooning Championships bound for Boyle
item.description: Hot-air balloon experts from across the world will once again descend on Lough Key Forest Park in Boyle in 2026. That's after it was confirmed earlier today that The Irish Hot Air Ballooning Championships will take place there next September. Thousands of people watched the experts earlier this year with photos circulating on social media. Advertisement The 2026 Championships will take place between the 19th and 25th September. item.title: Local domestic violence services allocated funding
item.description: A number of local domestic, sexual and gender-based violence services locally have been allocated funding. Today's announcement by Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan is part of an €3.2 million allocation in such services. Athlone Community Services Council CLG, which operates Esker House, has been awarded €15,000, while Athlone Rape Crisis Centre will receive just over €71,200. item.title: Brigid's and Scotstown set for Breffni Park
item.description: St. Brigid’s and Scotstown will meet in the All-Ireland club semi-final on Sunday January fourth in Kingspan Breffni at 3:30pm. The GAA announced details of the club championship fixtures this evening with Cavan announced as the venue for the meeting of the Roscommon and Monaghan champions. The other semi-final will see Kerry and Munster champions Dingle face Dublin and Leinster champions Ballyboden St. Enda’s in Pairc Ui Chaoimh on Saturday January third at 3:15pm.
